claim.pdf_says: Table 16 has a two-level header: a spanning cell 'Category of receiving operand' across all six data columns, above the individual column labels 'Alphabetic', 'Alphanumeric-edited, Alphanumeric', 'Boolean', 'National, National-edited', 'Numeric, Numeric-edited', 'Type-name'; the stub cell to its left reads 'Category of sending operand'.
claim.markdown_says: | Category of sending operand | | Alphabetic | Alphanumeric-edited, Alphanumeric | Boolean | National, National-edited | Numeric, Numeric-edited | Type-name |
claim.why_it_matters: The spanning header 'Category of receiving operand' is printed in the PDF but absent from the transcription. It is the label that identifies the column axis; without it the table is only interpretable by inferring the axis from the stub, and a reader consulting the table to decide whether a MOVE is legal has no printed statement of which axis is the receiving operand. The Yes/No body of the table was checked cell by cell against the PDF and is transcribed correctly.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED after independent render and read; I tried to refute it on all four grounds and could not.

(1) Not present elsewhere. I rendered p696 at 300dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v696/spec_p696.png) and read the printed glyphs directly. The table header is unambiguously two rows deep: a single bold cell reading 'Category of receiving operand' spans horizontally across all six data columns, immediately under the caption 'Table 16 - Validity of types of MOVE statements'; below it sit the six individual column labels. To the left, one tall cell spanning both header rows (and both stub columns) reads 'Category of sending operand'. I then grepped the canonical transcription: 'Category of receiving operand' occurs exactly ONCE in the whole of specs/ISO_COBOL.md, at line 28672, which is a DIFFERENT table (the figurative-constant table, where it is an ordinary single-row column label). It does not occur anywhere in or near the Table 16 block (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 28523-28536), nor on the adjacent page-695 slice (line 28515 is the cross-reference 'table 16, Validity of types of MOVE statements'), nor reflowed into a note. The text is genuinely gone.

(2) Not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation. The omitted string is a distinct header cell, not a running head, folio, or a wrap artifact. By contrast the PDF's second column label IS wrapped across three printed lines ('Alphanumeric' / '-edited,' / 'Alphanumeric') and the markdown correctly rejoins it as 'Alphanumeric-edited, Alphanumeric' - so the transcriber handled genuine wrapping correctly here, which isolates the missing span row as a real omission rather than a reflow artifact.

(3) Neither source is misquoted. The markdown quote in the claim matches specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 28525 byte for byte, including the empty second cell that stands in for the Integer/Noninteger sub-column. The PDF description matches what I see printed.

(4) It does change meaning, and the change is load-bearing. Table 16 is ASYMMETRIC, so the axis assignment decides conformance answers: row Alphabetic x column 'National, National-edited' = Yes, while row National x column Alphabetic = No; likewise row 'Numeric/Integer' x column 'National, National-edited' = Yes while row National-edited x column 'Numeric, Numeric-edited' = No. A reader who transposes the axes therefore gets the wrong legality verdict for those MOVEs. The surviving stub 'Category of sending operand' in the leftmost column is the only remaining disambiguator, and it is a weak one because the flattened markdown row places that stub in the same header row as the six receiving-category labels, which actively invites reading all seven as peer column labels of one axis. Nothing in the transcription states that the columns are the receiving operand.

One independent check beyond the claim: I re-verified the Yes/No body cell by cell against the render (Alphabetic: Yes Yes No Yes No No; Alphanumeric: Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes No; Alphanumeric-edited: Yes Yes No Yes No No; Boolean: No Yes Yes Yes No No; National: No No Yes Yes Yes No; National-edited: No No No Yes No No; Numeric/Integer: No Yes No Yes Yes No; Numeric/Noninteger: No No No No Yes No; Numeric-edited: No Yes No Yes Yes No; Type-name: Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes). All 60 cells and both Numeric sub-row labels transcribe correctly, confirming that part of the claim as well. The sole defect is the dropped spanning header.
verdict.corrected_description: The claim is accurate as filed; two refinements for the ledger. (a) Scope: only the SPANNING row is lost. The transcription does preserve the stub 'Category of sending operand' and does preserve the empty second column that carries the Integer/Noninteger sub-labels, so the row axis remains inferable - the omission is the printed column-axis label, not the whole header. In the PDF the stub cell spans two header rows AND both stub columns; the 'Category of receiving operand' cell spans the six data columns. (b) Impact, stated concretely: because Table 16 is asymmetric (Alphabetic -> National = Yes but National -> Alphabetic = No; Numeric/Integer -> National-edited = Yes but National-edited -> Numeric = No), a transposed reading yields wrong MOVE-legality verdicts, so this is a semantic loss and not merely cosmetic. Remedy note: a GFM pipe table cannot express a colspan, so the fix is to restore the label textually - e.g. rename the six column headers as 'Receiving: Alphabetic', ... or add an italic line above the table reading 'Columns: Category of receiving operand. Rows: Category of sending operand.' Severity 'structural' is appropriate.
